\section[la ganancia]{la ganancia — the gain, the profit}

\label{lesson:ES-C629-ganancia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the interest, then the Spanish for to withdraw.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la ganancia}
\textbf{la ganancia} — \textquotedblleft{}the gain, the profit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La tienda tuvo ganancias este año.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The shop made a profit this year.}
\end{quote}

Often plural: \emph{las ganancias}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ganancia} is built on \emph{ganar} 'to earn, to win', which was probably borrowed from Gothic \emph{ganan} 'to covet' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la ganancia}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la ganancia}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la ganancia}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the interest, then the Spanish for to withdraw, then say \emph{la ganancia} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la ganancia mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The gain, the profit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[la pérdida]{la pérdida — the loss}

\label{lesson:ES-C629-perdida}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to withdraw, then the Spanish for the gain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la pérdida}
\textbf{la pérdida} — \textquotedblleft{}the loss\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Fue una pérdida de tiempo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It was a waste of time.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Pérdida de tiempo} — a waste of time.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pérdida} is inherited from Late Latin \emph{perdita} 'lost', from \emph{perdere} 'to lose, to destroy' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la pérdida}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la pérdida}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la pérdida}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to withdraw, then the Spanish for the gain, then say \emph{la pérdida} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la pérdida mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The loss\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el beneficio]{el beneficio — the profit; the benefit}

\label{lesson:ES-C629-beneficio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the gain, then the Spanish for the loss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el beneficio}
\textbf{el beneficio} — \textquotedblleft{}the profit; the benefit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La empresa tuvo un beneficio de un millón.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The company made a profit of a million.}
\end{quote}

Also a benefit: \emph{en beneficio de todos} — for the good of all.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{beneficio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{beneficium} 'a kindness, a favour', built from \emph{bene} 'well' and \emph{facere} 'to do' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el beneficio}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el beneficio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el beneficio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the gain, then the Spanish for the loss, then say \emph{el beneficio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el beneficio mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The profit; the benefit\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la inversión]{la inversión — the investment}

\label{lesson:ES-C629-inversion}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the loss, then the Spanish for the profit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la inversión}
\textbf{la inversión} — \textquotedblleft{}the investment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La casa es una buena inversión.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The house is a good investment.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{invertir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{inversión} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{inversio} 'a turning about', built on \emph{invertere}, from \emph{vertere} 'to turn' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la inversión}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la inversión}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the loss, then the Spanish for the profit, then say \emph{la inversión} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la inversión mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The investment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[financiar]{financiar — to finance, to fund}

\label{lesson:ES-C629-financiar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the profit, then the Spanish for the investment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: financiar}
\textbf{financiar} — \textquotedblleft{}to finance, to fund\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El ayuntamiento financia el proyecto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The town council funds the project.}
\end{quote}

\emph{La financiación} — the funding.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{financiar} is built on \emph{finanzas}, borrowed from French \emph{finance} 'payment, settlement' (EtymDB), which is usually traced to Latin \emph{finis} 'end': to settle a debt was to end it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{financiar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{financiar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{financiar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the profit, then the Spanish for the investment, then say \emph{financiar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does financiar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To finance, to fund\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
